title: Counter circuits (binary, BCD, Johnson, ring)
summary: Counters are sequential circuits that count pulses. Types: binary counter (counts 0 to 2^n-1, then wraps), BCD counter (counts 0-9, then resets), Johnson counter (shift register with feedback, 2n states), ring counter (shift register with one 1, n states), up/down counter (can increment or decrement).

ext.summary: Counters are sequential circuits that count pulses. Types: binary counter (counts 0 to 2^n-1, then wraps), BCD counter (counts 0-9, then resets), Johnson counter (shift register with feedback, 2n states), ring counter (shift register with one 1, n states), up/down counter (can increment or decrement).

structure.meaning: Counts 0, 1, 2, ..., 2^n-1, 0. Uses T flip-flops with carry chain.
Counts 0-9, then resets to 0. Detects 1010 and resets.
Shift register with inverted feedback. Counts 2n states: 000...0, 100...0, 110...0, ..., 111...1, 011...1, ..., 000...1.
Shift register with one 1. Counts n states: 100...0, 010...0, ..., 000...1.
Counts up or down based on a direction input. Uses adder/subtractor logic.
All flip-flops clocked simultaneously. Faster than ripple (asynchronous) counter.
Each flip-flop clocks the next. Simpler but slower (carry ripples).

notes: Binary counters are used for address generation, timers, and frequency division.
Johnson counters are used for phase generation and sequencers.
Ring counters are used for one-hot state machines.
Counters are the basis of timers, PWM, and frequency synthesizers.
Synchronous counters are preferred for high-speed designs.
